do_more: Pick everyday, tangible objects (mug, raincoat, coffee) as the story anchor
Frame the concept as a paradox, surprise or certainty violation to spark curiosity
Start with a visual gag or hook in the first 3‑5 seconds
Keep the runtime around 40‑45 seconds (standard length)
Use the "The X Y" title pattern that names the object and the twist
avoid: Abstract or overly academic phrasing in titles
Choosing niche topics that lack immediate visual comedy potential
Running videos under 30 seconds unless the joke lands instantly
short.title_style: Use a simple "The [Everyday Object] [Paradox/Contradiction]" format that promises a surprising twist
next_tests: Create tight 30‑second versions of the top‑performing concepts to see if brevity boosts VPD
Add a bold, question‑style hook in the first 2 seconds (e.g., "Ever wondered why your mug never empties?")
Experiment with titles that pose a direct curiosity question instead of a statement, like "Why does a raincoat feel certain?"
